arxiv-1912-03655.title: Invariant spectral foliations with applications to model order reduction and synthesis
arxiv-1912-03655.creator: Robert Szalai
arxiv-1912-03655.description: Abstract The paper introduces a technique that decomposes the dynamics of a nonlinear system about an equilibrium into low order components, which then can be used to reconstruct the full dynamics. This is a nonlinear analogue of linear modal analysis.

arxiv-2103-04518.title: “Sharks are not the threat humans are”: Argument Component Segmentation in School Student Essays
arxiv-2103-04518.creator: Tariq Alhindi, Debanjan Ghosh
arxiv-2103-04518.description: Abstract Argument mining is often addressed by a pipeline method where segmentation of text into argumentative units is conducted first and proceeded by an argument component identification task. In this research, we apply a token-level classification to identify claim and premise tokens from a new corpus of argumentative essays written by middle school students.

arxiv-2104-08997.title: Masked Face Recognition using ResNet-50
arxiv-2104-08997.creator: Bishwas Mandal, Adaeze Okeukwu, Yihong Theis
arxiv-2104-08997.description: Abstract Over the last twenty years, there have seen several outbreaks of different coronavirus diseases across the world. These outbreaks often led to respiratory tract diseases and have proved to be fatal sometimes. Currently, we are facing an elusive health crisis with the emergence of COVID-19 disease of the coronavirus family.

arxiv-2104-13328.title: The hydrodynamic characteristics of Autonomous Underwater Vehicles in rotating flow fields Journal: Ocean Engineering
arxiv-2104-13328.creator: A. Mitra, J.P. Panda, H.V. Warrior
arxiv-2104-13328.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by A. Mitra, J.P. Panda, H.V. Warrior. In this article, the hydrodynamic characteristics of Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) are investigated and analyzed under the influence of rotating flow fields, that were generated in a recirculating water tank via a rotating propeller. Initially, experiments were carried out for the measurement of flow field variables and Quantities of Interest across the AUV in the presence of the rotating propeller while varying the rotational speed and the extent of rotational flow strength.

arxiv-2201-09439.title: A Reilly type integral formula and its applications Thanks: The research of authors is supported by NSFC(No. 11971153).
arxiv-2201-09439.creator: Guangyue Huang, Bingqing Ma, Mingfang Zhu
arxiv-2201-09439.description: Abstract . In this paper, we achieve a Reilly type integral formula associated with the ϕ \phi -Laplacian. As its applications, we obtain Heintze-Karcher and Minkowski type inequalities. Furthermore, almost Schur lemmas are also given. They recover the partial results of Li and Xia in [ 15 ] .

arxiv-2202-08404.title: Global-in-time existence of weak solutions for Vlasov–Manev–Fokker–Planck system
arxiv-2202-08404.creator: Young-Pil Choi, In-Jee Jeong
arxiv-2202-08404.description: Abstract We consider the Vlasov–Manev–Fokker–Planck (VMFP) system in three dimensions, which differs from the Vlasov–Poisson–Fokker–Planck in that it has the gravitational potential of the form − 1 / r − 1 / r 2 -1/r-1/r^{2} instead of the Newtonian one. For the VMFP system, we establish the global-in-time existence of weak solutions. The proof extends to several related kinetic systems.

arxiv-2308-10037.title: High Performance Computing Applied to Logistic Regression: A CPU and GPU Implementation Comparison
arxiv-2308-10037.creator: MOHAMED MOUHAJIR, MOHAMMED NECHBA, YASSINE SEDJARI
arxiv-2308-10037.description: Abstract We present a versatile GPU-based parallel version of Logistic Regression (LR), aiming to address the increasing demand for faster algorithms in binary classification due to large data sets. Our implementation is a direct translation of the parallel Gradient Descent Logistic Regression algorithm proposed by X. Zou et al. [ 12 ] .

arxiv-2312-07047.title: Low-energy limit of N-photon amplitudes in a constant field
arxiv-2312-07047.creator: Naser Ahmadiniaz, Misha A. Lopez-Lopez, Christian Schubert
arxiv-2312-07047.description: Abstract While the QED photon amplitudes at full momentum so far have been calculated only up to the six-photon level, in the low-energy limit there are explicit formulas for all helicity components even at the N N -photon level, obtained by Martin et al. in 2002.

arxiv-2401-07295.title: θ \theta -Lebesgue spaces
arxiv-2401-07295.creator: Shouvik Datta Choudhury
arxiv-2401-07295.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Shouvik Datta Choudhury. Traditional L p L_{p} spaces are fundamental in functional analysis, demarcated by the relationship 1 / p + 1 / q = 1 1/p+1/q=1 . This research pioneers the concept of θ \theta -Lebesgue space, stemming from a simultaneous weakening of both the classical L p L_{p} relation and its θ \theta -variant, 1 / ( θ ⁡ ( p ) ) + 1 / ( θ ⁡ ( q ) ) = 1 1/(\theta(p))+1/(\theta(q))=1 .

arxiv-2503-20413.title: Zippy– Generic White-Box Proof Search with Zippers
arxiv-2503-20413.creator: Kevin Kappelmann
arxiv-2503-20413.description: Abstract We present a framework for tree-based proof search, called Zippy. Unlike existing proof search tools, Zippy is largely independent of concrete search tree representations, search-algorithms, states and effects. It is designed to create analysable and navigable proof searches that are open to customisation and extensions by users.

arxiv-2509-17718.title: Probing Long-Lived Photophobic Axion-Like Particles via Prompt Leptons and Mono- γ \gamma at FCC-ee and CEPC
arxiv-2509-17718.creator: Shi-Yu Wang a, Yu-Peng Jiao a, Hong-Hao Zhang a, Giacomo Cacciapaglia b
arxiv-2509-17718.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Shi-Yu Wang a, Yu-Peng Jiao a, Hong-Hao Zhang a, Giacomo Cacciapaglia b. We investigate the potential to probe axion-like particles (ALPs) under the photophobic scenario at the FCC-ee and CEPC at the Z-pole, with s = 91.2 \sqrt{s}=91.2 GeV.

arxiv-2511-09220.title: Weak conditional propagation of chaos for systems of interacting particles with nearly stable jumps
arxiv-2511-09220.creator: Eva Löcherbach ??, Dasha Loukianova ??, Elisa Marini ??
arxiv-2511-09220.description: Abstract We consider a system of N N interacting particles, described by SDEs driven by Poisson random measures, where the coefficients depend on the empirical measure of the system. Every particle jumps with a jump rate depending on its position.

arxiv-2511-13937.title: Complex-Weighted Convolutional Networks: Provable Expressiveness via Complex Diffusion Thanks: and Mathematical bioPhysics Group, Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences Thanks: Max Planck Institute of Molecular Cell Biology and Genetics, Max Planck Institute for the Physics of Complex S
arxiv-2511-13937.creator: Cristina López Amado, Tassilo Schwarz, Yu Tian, Renaud Lambiotte
arxiv-2511-13937.description: Abstract Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have achieved remarkable success across diverse applications, yet they remain limited by oversmoothing and poor performance on heterophilic graphs. To address these challenges, we introduce a novel framework that equips graphs with a complex-weighted structure, assigning each edge a complex number to drive a diffusion process that extends random walks into the complex domain.

arxiv-2601-10190.title: Exponential Analysis for Entanglement Distillation
arxiv-2601-10190.creator: Zhiwen Lin, Ke Li, Kun Fang
arxiv-2601-10190.description: Abstract Historically, the focus in entanglement distillation has predominantly been on the distillable entanglement, and the framework assumes complete knowledge of the initial state. In this paper, we study the reliability function of entanglement distillation, which specifies the optimal exponent of the decay of the distillation error when the distillation rate is below the distillable entanglement.

plos-pone-0002684.description: PLOS ONE research article. The World Health Organization (WHO) released new Child Growth Standards in 2006 to replace the current National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS) growth reference. We assessed how switching from the NCHS to the newly released WHO Growth Standards affects the estimated prevalenc

pmc-10663755.title: Genetic relationship between the immune system and autism
pmc-10663755.creator: Martina Arenella, Giuseppe Fanelli, Lambertus A Kiemeney, Grainne McAlonan, Declan G Murphy, Janita Bralten
pmc-10663755.description: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a common and complex neurodevelopmental condition. The pathophysiology of ASD is poorly defined; however, it includes a strong genetic component and there is increasing evidence to support a role of immune dysregulation. Nonetheless, it is unclear which immune phenotypes link to ASD through genetics.

pmc-10751762.title: Early-Onset Parkinson Mutation Remodels Monomer–Fibril Interactions to Allosterically Amplify Synuclein’s Amyloid Cascade
pmc-10751762.creator: Jinfeng Huang, Rashik Ahmed, Madoka Akimoto, Karla Martinez Pomier, Giuseppe Melacini
pmc-10751762.description: Alpha synuclein (αS) aggregates are the main component of Lewy bodies (LBs) associated with Parkinson’s disease (PD). A longstanding question about αS and PD pertains to the autosomal dominant E46K αS mutant, which leads to the early onset of PD and LB dementias.

pmc-11322527.title: Synergistic pectin deconstruction is a prerequisite for mutualistic interactions between honeybee gut bacteria
pmc-11322527.creator: Junbo Tang, Wenlong Zuo, Lizhen Guo, Zhihao Han, Chengfeng Yang, Benfeng Han, Lei Dai, Xue Zhang, Xin Zhou
pmc-11322527.description: The honeybee gut microbiome is crucial for degrading diverse pollen glycans. Yet it is unclear how this process shapes the interactions among bacteria. Here, we demonstrate a conditional mutualistic interaction between strains of two honeybee gut bacteria Bifidobacterium asteroides and Gilliamella apicola.

pmc-11402205.title: A psychosocial bouldering intervention improves the well-being of young refugees and adolescents from the host community in Lebanon: results from a pragmatic controlled trial
pmc-11402205.creator: Katharina Luttenberger, Beat Baggenstos, Charbel Najem, Charles Sifri, Piotr Lewczuk, Anne Radegast, Simon Rosenbaum
pmc-11402205.description: BackgroundMental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) is increasingly considered vital for addressing the needs of displaced communities. The mental health of young people in Lebanon, including members of the host community and refugees, has been severely affected by multiple crises.

pmc-11405868.title: Highly efficient CRISPR-mediated genome editing through microfluidic droplet cell mechanoporation
pmc-11405868.creator: You-Jeong Kim, Dayoung Yun, Jungjoon K Lee, Cheulhee Jung, Aram J Chung
pmc-11405868.description: Clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-based editing tools have transformed the landscape of genome editing. However, the absence of a robust and safe CRISPR delivery method continues to limit its potential for therapeutic applications. Despite the emergence of various methodologies aimed at addressing this challenge, issues regarding efficiency and editing operations persist.

pmc-11431302.title: Quantifying Treatments as Usual and with Technologies in Neurorehabilitation of Individuals with Spinal Cord Injury
pmc-11431302.creator: Federica Tamburella, Matteo Lorusso, Mario Merone, Luca Bacco, Marco Molinari, Marco Tramontano, Giorgio Scivoletto, Nevio Luigi Tagliamonte, Kaux Jean-François
pmc-11431302.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Several technologies have been introduced into neurorehabilitation programs to enhance traditional treatment of individuals with Spinal Cord Injury (SCI). Their effectiveness has been widely investigated, but their adoption has not been properly quantified. The aim of this study is to assess the distribution of conventional (Treatment As Usual—TAU) and technology-aided (Treatment With Technologies—TWT) treatments conveniently grouped based on different therapeutic goals in a selected SCI unit.

pmc-11485154.title: Scopus Search Analyzer
pmc-11485154.creator: Mackenzie Hilton
pmc-11485154.description: representations that help users visualize the bibliometrics of their search. Pie charts, line graphs, and bar graphs – all colour coded – simplify complex data and allow researchers to identify trends, relevant journals and scholars, and overlap with other subjects. Intended users Scopus’ search analyzer is intended for research at any stage, from background research to systematic reviews.

pmc-11604964.title: Nonthermal fluctuations accelerate biomolecular motors
pmc-11604964.creator: Takayuki Ariga
pmc-11604964.description: Intracellular transport is essential for maintaining cellular function. This process is driven by different mechanisms in prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells. In small prokaryotic cells, diffusion is the primary means of transport, while larger eukaryotic cells also rely on active transport by molecular motors such as kinesin and dynein.

pmc-12541059.title: Exploring salinity-induced biochemical changes in Chlorella vulgaris using statistical modelling
pmc-12541059.creator: Ana F Esteves, Ana L Gonçalves, Vítor J P Vilar, José C M Pires
pmc-12541059.description: The impact of high salinity stress on the growth and nutrient uptake of Chlorella vulgaris was investigated using a two-stage cultivation approach. Changes in the biochemical composition of the biomass were statistically evaluated through principal component analysis (PCA) and multiple linear regression (MLR).

pmc-12824088.title: Evaluation of drug options for epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) treatment using the analytical hierarchy process improves decision-making transparency
pmc-12824088.creator: Hamzeh Ghorbani, Tatevik Arshakyan, Arsen Minasyan, Simin Ghorbani, David A. Wood, Nina Khlghatyan, Parvin Ghorbani, Eduard Avagyan
pmc-12824088.description: Epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) poses considerable challenges in selecting appropriate treatments due to the interplay of factors such as drug efficacy, safety, cost, resistance, and patient compliance. To address these complexities, this study employs the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) as a structured and transparent decision-making framework for evaluating and ranking drug therapies for EOC.

pmc-13173208.title: 184 Developing quantitative writing evaluations for TL1 scientific writing programs
pmc-13173208.creator: Jen Merems, David Puthoff, Leigh A. Mrotek, Xudong Wang, Vivek Prabhakaran, Bernadette T. Gillick
pmc-13173208.description: Objectives/Goals: Scientific writing is vital for TL1 trainees, yet evaluating writing programs effectiveness is challenging. Current evaluations gauge writing confidence, not skill competency. Our study aimed to develop a quantitative writing evaluation tool to assess technique and improvement longitudinally across the TL1 program. Methods/Study Population: The writing evaluation tool uses 19 typical grammar concepts embedded within three paragraphs.

pmc-13485880.title: Editorial: Emerging fast medical imaging techniques in radiology
pmc-13485880.creator: Zhifeng Chen, Zhicheng Peng, Mingfeng Jiang, Jianfeng Zhou, Lijun Lu, Xiaoyun Liang
pmc-13485880.description: on (12, 13), algorithmic reconstruction (11, 14, 15), and artificial intelligence (AI) (2, 3, 10, 16), have become central to modern radiology. This Research Topic, “Emerging Fast Medical Imaging Techniques in Radiology,” brings together 15 articles across several Frontiers journals. Collectively, these contributions underscore the rapid evolution and expanding scope of cutting-edge imaging methodologies in clinical practice.
